name: Nostril Darkness
description: Assesses nostril cavity shading depth and bilateral luminance symmetry, targeting a fine-detail region where generative models frequently produce physically implausible shadow gradients.
mechanism:
This method analyzes nostril darkness and rendering for deepfake detection:

1. **Nostril Detection**: The nostrils are detected per frame as dark interior regions visible at the base of the nose. Their shape (typically oval), size, and darkness level are measured.

2. **Darkness Level Analysis**: Natural nostrils show very low luminance (dark cavity) with specific spectral properties (warm dark due to skin back-scattering). The method measures nostril darkness and compares against expected values. AI generators may produce nostrils that are: too bright (failing to render the cavity), too uniform (lacking internal light gradients), or with incorrect color temperature.

3. **Bilateral Symmetry**: Left and right nostrils should be approximately symmetric in size and darkness (adjusted for head pose). The method checks bilateral nostril consistency. AI generators may produce asymmetric nostrils or nostrils that change relative size between frames.

4. **Pose-Dependent Visibility**: Nostril visibility changes predictably with head pitch — looking up shows more nostril interior, looking down hides them. The method verifies that nostril appearance changes correctly with estimated head pose. Incorrect pose-dependent nostril rendering indicates AI generation.

5. **Temporal Nostril Stability**: Nostril dark regions should maintain consistent shape and position across frames (nostrils don't move relative to nose). The method tracks nostril features over time. Frame-to-frame nostril instability — changing shape, flickering darkness, shifting position — indicates per-frame independent rendering.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through nostril darkness analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
